summary: 18 T1 tests, correct tier (MemoryBinStore + an injected TestClock, no sleep, no port, no temp dir, a fake rather than a mock), independent (a fresh store and clock per test), well named. The expiry boundary, the epoch-advance-by-one, the release-does-not-delete pair, the fenced-release, and the corrupt-lease-is-loud behaviours are all genuinely pinned -- I killed each with a mutation. But THE CONDITIONAL WRITE ITSELF -- the one property that makes a lease a lease -- is unconstrained on every path, and the version bookkeeping after a winning CAS is unconstrained on two of three. Three MAJOR surviving mutations, each verified green over all 18 tests and each verified non-equivalent by a probe test that passes on the unmutated code and fails on the mutant: (1) putIfAbsent -> unconditional put on first acquisition; (2) renew() not advancing heldVersion on success, so a holder can renew exactly once; (3) the takeover path recording the PRE-takeover version, so a node that fails over can never renew. Consequences are two nodes sequencing at once and cluster-wide loss of sequencing respectively -- exactly the failures this class exists to prevent. `adopt`'s lost-race branch is DEAD in the suite: replacing its `return Optional.empty()` with `throw new AssertionError` leaves all 18 green, which is the mechanical statement of the same hole. Judging the two reds the packet flags: the release no-op red is meaningful (it asserts counts().total() is ZERO, not merely 'no throw'); the renew-without-acquiring red is meaningful but weaker (emptiness only, no request-count assertion, unlike its sibling). Backlog row is honest on the numbers -- I re-ran the whole suite and measured exactly 472 -- but one clause it states as delivered has no test at all. Working tree restored; `git diff` is empty and the staged bytes still hash to ff3aee50.

findings.title: Neither acquisition path's CONDITIONAL write is constrained: `putIfAbsent` -> unconditional `put` survives all 18 tests, and `adopt`'s lost-race branch is dead code in the suite
findings.failure_scenario: MEASURED, twice. (a) Mutate LeaseManager.java:122 `adopt(fresh, store.putIfAbsent(key, Body.ofBytes(fresh.encode())))` to `adopt(fresh, Optional.of(store.put(key, Body.ofBytes(fresh.encode()))))`: `./gradlew :sequencer:test --tests binjava.sequencer.LeaseManagerTest` exits 0, 18/18 green. The test named `theFirstAcquisitionUsesPutIfAbsentBecausePutIfMatchThrowsOnAnAbsentKey` asserts only `store.counts().puts() == 1`, and an unconditional PUT is also exactly one write -- the name carries the claim, the assertion does not. (b) Mutate LeaseManager.java:191-192, `adopt`'s `if (won.isEmpty()) { return Optional.empty(); }`, to `throw new AssertionError("DEAD BRANCH")`: still 18/18 green, so NO test in the file ever exercises a LOSING acquisition CAS on either path. `exactlyOneOfTwoContendersAcquiresAnUnheldLease` (line 94) does not cover it: B's `stat` finds the object present, so B is refused by the EXPIRY check at LeaseManager.java:128 and never reaches a conditional write at all. Consequence of (a) in production: two ingesters starting against a fresh prefix both see `stat` empty, both PUT, both are told they hold epoch 0, and both sequence -- the split brain the whole class exists to prevent, and the exact reason the SPI has `putIfAbsent`. VERIFIED NON-EQUIVALENT: a 10-line T1 test kills it -- wrap the shared MemoryBinStore in a BinStore whose `stat` always returns Optional.empty() (the concurrent window, deterministically), hand it to B after A has acquired, and assert B's `tryAcquire()` is empty and `Lease.decode(shared.get(key).readAllBytes())` still equals A's lease. That test passes on the unmutated code and fails under the mutant; I ran both.

findings.title: No test renews TWICE, so `renew()` failing to advance `heldVersion` on a winning CAS survives -- a holder that can renew exactly once then believes itself fenced forever
findings.failure_scenario: MEASURED. Delete `heldVersion = won.get();` from LeaseManager.java:161 (keep `held = renewed`): all 18 tests green, exit 0. Both renew tests call `renew()` exactly once -- `theHolderRenewsWithoutChangingTheEpoch` (130) and `aFencedHolderCannotRenewAndLearnsItFromTheEmptyResult` (144) -- so the steady state, which is the single most-executed path in this class (one CAS every renewInterval for the life of the pod), is never entered. Consequence in production: the second renew CASes against a version the first renew already superseded, `putIfMatch` returns empty, the holder takes that as proof it is fenced (exactly as the javadoc instructs) and STOPS SEQUENCING, every renewInterval, forever -- the cluster hands leadership back and forth and never commits. Note this is worse than a silent bug: it is indistinguishable at the call site from real fencing. VERIFIED NON-EQUIVALENT: a probe that acquires and then loops five renews, advancing the clock by RENEW each time and asserting `isPresent()`, passes on the unmutated code (exit 0) and fails under the mutant (exit 1). Fix is one loop in the existing renew test.

findings.title: The takeover path's recorded version is unconstrained: adopting the PRE-takeover version survives all 18 tests, so a node that fails over can never renew
findings.failure_scenario: MEASURED. Replace LeaseManager.java:132-133 with `Optional<Version> won = store.putIfMatch(key, Body.ofBytes(taken.encode()), stat.get().version()); return adopt(taken, won.isEmpty() ? won : Optional.of(stat.get().version()));` -- i.e. the CAS still happens and still wins, but the manager records the version it CASed FROM rather than the one it CASed TO. All 18 tests green, exit 0. No test in the file ever renews after a TAKEOVER: `anExpiredLeaseIsTakenOverAndTheEpochAdvancesByExactlyOne` (114) throws the taking-over manager away after one assertion, and every successful renew in the file follows a FIRST acquisition. Consequence in production: failover appears to succeed -- the new holder returns a lease at epoch N+1 and starts sequencing -- and then its very first renew loses, it concludes it is fenced and stops, so the cluster loses sequencing for a full TTL on every failover and then repeats. VERIFIED NON-EQUIVALENT: a probe (A acquires, clock advances TTL, B takes over, clock advances RENEW, assert `b.renew()` isPresent) passes on the unmutated code and fails under the mutant; I ran both. Fix is three lines added to the existing takeover test.

findings.title: The backlog row's 'the local belief is dropped with it' clause has no test -- deleting the two clearing lines from renew()'s fenced branch survives all 18 tests (testing.md rule 13)
findings.failure_scenario: MEASURED. Delete `held = null; heldVersion = null;` from LeaseManager.java:156-157: 18/18 green, exit 0. `aFencedHolderCannotRenewAndLearnsItFromTheEmptyResult` asserts only that the FIRST renew after fencing is empty, which the mutant also satisfies. The backlog row states this as delivered behaviour in its own words -- 'the local belief is dropped with it so a caller ignoring the result cannot keep renewing against a stale version' -- and the javadoc at LeaseManager.java:155 repeats it, so this is an acceptance claim with nothing constraining it. Kept at minor rather than major only because the observable consequence today is bounded: `held()` would report a lease the instance does not hold, and `held()` has no caller (see the next finding), while a further renew or release against the stale version simply loses its CAS. It becomes a real defect the moment M5 or M8 asks 'am I the leader'. Fix: assert `a.held()` is empty and a SECOND `a.renew()` is still empty after the fencing.

findings.title: `held()` is entirely unconstrained -- returning `Optional.empty()` unconditionally survives all 18 tests
findings.failure_scenario: MEASURED. Mutate `return Optional.ofNullable(held);` to `return Optional.empty();`: 18/18 green, exit 0. No test calls `held()`. It is a public accessor on the class that answers 'who may write the commit chain', shipped with zero constraint -- which is precisely testing.md rule 8's case of a line that will be counted as covered (it is not even that, it is uncovered) while constraining nothing. Same family as the previous finding: the cheapest fix closes both, since asserting `held()` before and after a fencing kills the empty-constant mutant AND the missing-clear mutant in one test. Related and also unconstrained: deleting `held = null; heldVersion = null;` from `release()` at LeaseManager.java:180-181 likewise leaves 18/18 green.

findings.title: The cost test names an acquire cost it never asserts, and the name it does carry is true of only one of three acquire paths
findings.failure_scenario: MEASURED. `acquiringCostsOneReadAndOneWriteAndRenewingCostsOneWrite` takes `afterAcquire = store.counts().total()` as a BASELINE and asserts only the renew DELTA, so nothing constrains the acquire half. Insert `store.stat(key);` immediately before LeaseManager.java:121: all 18 tests green, exit 0 -- a redundant, billed request on the first-acquisition path is invisible. Consequence is bounded (acquisition is not the rate-carrying operation; renewal is, and that half IS pinned, which is the half cost.md cares about), hence minor. Two further accuracy notes on the name, which under cost.md rule 22 is part of the assertion: the 'one read' is a `stat`, not a `get`; and only the FIRST acquisition costs 2 -- a takeover costs 3 (stat + get + putIfMatch) and a refused acquire costs 2 (stat + get), neither of which is asserted anywhere. Fix: assert `afterAcquire` equals 2 with `.as(...)`, and add the takeover and refusal counts, which would also close the cost half of the takeover gap in finding 3.

findings.title: `aNonPositiveTtlIsRefused` tests only ZERO, and the renewInterval positivity guard is unconstrained entirely
findings.failure_scenario: MEASURED, twice. (a) Mutate LeaseManager.java:72 `if (ttl.isZero() || ttl.isNegative())` to `if (ttl.isZero())`: 18/18 green, exit 0 -- the test's own name says NON-POSITIVE but its only input is `Duration.ZERO`. A negative TTL is then accepted and every lease is born already expired, so the holder is stealable the instant it acquires. (b) Delete the whole `renewInterval.isZero() || renewInterval.isNegative()` block at LeaseManager.java:75-78: 18/18 green. The surviving `renewInterval.compareTo(ttl) >= 0` check at line 79 does NOT catch a negative, so a negative renewInterval is accepted and handed straight back out by `renewInterval()` to whatever loop M8 builds. Both are one extra `assertThatThrownBy` line. Credit where due: the equal-durations case at line 247 does pin the `>=` boundary -- mutating it to `> 0` is killed.

findings.title: `holderEndpoint` is plumbed through the constructor but never asserted -- replacing it with a literal "" survives all 18 tests
findings.failure_scenario: MEASURED. Replace `endpoint` with `""` in BOTH Lease constructions (LeaseManager.java:121 and 131): 18/18 green, exit 0, because every test passes `""` for the endpoint. No assertion in the file mentions `holderEndpoint`. Harmless in M4 by construction -- M4.3's row says the field is deliberately EMPTY here -- which is why this is minor; but that same row justifies carrying the field at all by M5's commit forwarding, 'which must REACH the holder', and M5 will inherit a plumbing path that no test has ever constrained. One test constructing a manager with a non-empty endpoint and asserting it round-trips onto the acquired lease closes it now, while it is free.

findings.title: `renewingWithoutEverHavingAcquiredIsRefused` -- its red IS meaningful, but it is the weaker of the two the packet flags: emptiness only, no request count
findings.failure_scenario: JUDGED, with a measurement. The red is real: deleting the `if (held == null) return Optional.empty();` guard at LeaseManager.java:145-147 kills this test (1 failure), so it does constrain the guard's existence -- and it pins the guard's SHAPE too, that a non-holder renewing gets an empty Optional rather than an NPE or an exception, which is behaviour a caller relies on. But compare its sibling `releasingWhenNotHeldIsAHarmlessNoOpRatherThanAnError` (197), which asserts `store.counts().total()` is ZERO: that one additionally refuses any implementation that issues a request before returning empty. This one does not, so `if (held == null) { store.stat(key); return Optional.empty(); }` survives it -- a non-holder polling the store on every renew tick, which cost.md's zero-idle-request rule exists to prevent. Mirroring the release test's CountingBinStore assertion is a two-line change and makes the pair symmetric. The release test itself I judge fully meaningful and would not change.

verified: FULL SUITE: ./gradlew test exit 0; counted 472 tests by summing the tests= attribute over every build/test-results/test/*.xml. The backlog row's '472 tests green' is HONEST.
KILLED (test does its job) -- takenOverBy -> renewedUntil in tryAcquire: 2 failures. The epoch-advance-by-exactly-one is genuinely pinned.

KILLED -- isExpiredAt(clock.millis()) -> isExpiredAt(clock.millis() + 1) (steal 1ms early): 1 failure, caught by aHeldUnexpiredLeaseIsNotStolen. Both ends of the boundary are pinned: -> isExpiredAt(clock.millis() - 1) (expiry exclusive) gives 5 failures.

KILLED -- release() deleting the object (store.delete(List.of(key))) instead of writing an expired lease: 2 failures. releaseKeepsTheEpochSoTheNextHolderStillAdvancesIt does catch the epoch reset, as the row claims.
KILLED -- release() using an unconditional put instead of putIfMatch: 1 failure, caught by aFencedHolderCannotReleaseSomeoneElsesLease. The fenced-release half is genuinely pinned.
KILLED -- catching the IOException from read() in tryAcquire and treating a corrupt lease as unheld (taking it over): 1 failure. The corrupt-lease-is-loud behaviour is genuinely pinned.
KILLED -- release() writing an expiry of clock.millis() + 1 instead of clock.millis(): 2 failures. The INCLUSIVE-expiry boundary on the release side is pinned.
KILLED -- deleting renew()'s `if (held == null)` guard: 1 failure.

SURVIVED (findings above) -- putIfAbsent -> put; adopt's lost-race branch as an AssertionError; renew() not advancing heldVersion; takeover adopting the pre-takeover version; renew() not clearing held/heldVersion when fenced; release() not clearing them; held() -> Optional.empty(); a redundant stat on the first-acquisition path; dropping ttl.isNegative(); deleting the renewInterval positivity guard; endpoint -> "".

TIER: T1 is right -- MemoryBinStore plus an injected Clock, no socket, no real clock, no I/O the logic needs. Non-negotiable 7 is satisfied by the class taking Clock as a constructor parameter, and the tests exercise that (TestClock is ADVANCED, never slept on). No design finding.

testing.md: no Thread.sleep, no fixed port, no system temp, a fake (TestClock, MemoryBinStore) rather than a mock (rule 18), one behaviour per name (rule 12), failure paths present (rule 14: corrupt lease, fenced renew, fenced release, three constructor refusals). Tests are independent -- every one builds its own store and clock, and the only shared state is two Duration constants.
NO EXISTING ASSERTION WEAKENED: both new files are additions (A/A), and the only modified file is backlog.md. Nothing to invert.

BACKLOG HONESTY: the row's claims about release (both halves plus the fenced third), the corrupt lease, the two acquisition paths existing, the renewInterval refusal and the 472 count all check out. The clause 'the local belief is dropped with it so a caller ignoring the result cannot keep renewing against a stale version' does NOT -- see finding 4. The row does not claim mutation verification, which given the above is the honest omission.

TREE RESTORED: every mutation was reverted; `git diff` is empty, `git status --short` shows only the three staged paths, and `git diff --cached | sha256sum` still yields ff3aee50603e2ea221340171736b14126462d8dc3d303c973cf39135dc49c50b. Two temporary probe test files were created under sequencer/src/test and deleted.
